_comment: TEMPLATE for webkit.config.json — JSON has no comments, hence this key. The install step copies this file to webkit/webkit.config.json (same directory) and fills in real values for the project. scripts/config-get.sh falls back to THIS template whenever no webkit.config.json exists, so every value below is a working demo default, not a broken placeholder. Fill in: project_name (short slug), site_root (the preview server's DOCUMENT ROOT — the directory it serves, relative to the project root; the server os.chdir's here and serves it; it is NOT where the feedback inbox lives), default_page (path under site_root), lock_dir (per-project color registry, conventionally /tmp/<project_name>-agent-colors — point it at an EXISTING registry, e.g. another repo's, only if you want agents across repos to share one palette). palette[] is the single source of truth for colors: order = claim order, slug = filesystem-safe lock name, port = that color's preview-server port. browser.mode: auto (macOS+osascript => applescript, else print) | applescript | print; browser.app_name must be a Chromium-family app (shared AppleScript dictionary). feedback_dir is where per-color feedback rounds live, resolved relative to the GIT ROOT (not site_root) because BEFORE mode reads history via git — a subdir-site project still keeps its inbox at <git-root>/<feedback_dir>/<slug>/ (gitignored). The server binds 127.0.0.1 (localhost only) so the working tree and feedback intake are never exposed to the LAN; set an optional bind_host to override only for deliberate LAN use. hotkeys is OPTIONAL and overrides the overlay's two bare-key shortcuts: toggle (show/hide the feedback overlay, default "KeyC") and dictate (start/stop speech-to-text in the open note, default "KeyV"). Values are KeyboardEvent.code names ("Backquote", "KeyV", "Digit1", …), NOT characters — codes are keyboard-layout independent, which is what makes the shortcut work on a Hebrew (or any non-US) layout. The toggle key is the ONLY way to show/hide the overlay — there is deliberately no on-screen button — and it always wins, including inside a half-typed note, so whatever you pick cannot be typed as a literal character into feedback text. Pick a key you never need to type.
